title: Los Angeles weather: Rain moves through Southern California, creeps into Halloween forecast. Here's what to expect this weekend - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Rain moves through Southern California, creeps into Halloween forecast. Here's what to expect this weekend - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 Rain moves through SoCal, creeps into Halloween forecast. Here's what to expect 
 Los Angeles and Southern California are expected to see a wet Halloween weekend for the first time since 2014 as rain arrives into the region. Friday, October 30, 2026 4:19PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google Este artículo se ofrece en Español LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Rain moved into parts of Southern California on Friday as the region prepared for a potentially wet Halloween weekend, while coastal communities continued monitoring elevated tides and minor flooding concerns.
 ABC7 has issued a weather change alert due to the wet forecast.
 According to the National Weather Service, the main storm is expected to move eastward toward Southern California by Saturday afternoon and evening before pushing inland on Sunday.
 Current projections show rain arriving Saturday afternoon, potentially disrupting trick-or-treating and making it the first wet Halloween in Los Angeles since 2014.
 Rain is expected to continue through most of Sunday before conditions begin to clear Monday.
 Along the coast, high tides and flooding concerns remain in place Friday, although tide levels are not expected to reach those seen earlier in the week. Expect late-morning high tides between 6 and 7 feet.
 A coastal flood advisory remains in effect for beaches in Los Angeles, Orange and Ventura counties and is set to expire at 2 p.m. Friday.
 Friday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties are expected to see a 30% chance of showers Friday, with a high of 70 degrees and a low of 62. Up to three-quarters of an inch of rain could fall from late Saturday afternoon into Sunday morning.
 The valleys and Inland Empire Friday will see a high of 71 degrees and a low of 58, with a 30% chance for showers. Rain chances increase to 70% on Saturday, with rainfall totals expected to range from one-half inch to 1 inch.
 Beaches can expect a slight chance of showers, with a high of 68 degrees and a low of 59 on Friday. Surf is expected to be between 2 and 5 feet. Most rainfall is expected Saturday evening through Sunday morning, with up to one-half inch possible.
 Mountain communities will see a high of 51 degrees and a chilly overnight low of 34 on Friday. Cloudy skies and light showers are expected, with additional rain possible Saturday night into Sunday morning.
 Desert areas Friday can expect a high of 69 degrees and a low of 45, with partly sunny conditions. There's a 50% chance for rain on Saturday.
